title: Goodwill Share of the Refundable Fee Pool on Fee-Burdened Savings Accounts
content:
The goodwill share taken of the refundable fee pool on an account of Savings & Money Market Accounts rises with the fee burden the account has carried. Two facts decide it: the count of fee entries posted to the account in the twelve calendar months ending on the review date, and the whole months the account has been open.

Where 5 or more fee entries posted in that window and the account has been open no more than 12 whole months, the goodwill share is nine tenths of the refundable fee pool, that is 0.90 of it.

Where 3 or 4 fee entries posted in that window and the account has been open no more than 12 whole months, the goodwill share is three quarters of the refundable fee pool, that is 0.75 of it.

Where fewer than 3 fee entries posted in that window, or the account has been open more than 12 whole months, the goodwill share stays at one half of the refundable fee pool, that is 0.50 of it.

### The three shares on one pool

Take a hypothetical refundable fee pool of 30.00 USD. At nine tenths the share comes to 27.00 USD, at three quarters to 22.50 USD, and at one half to 15.00 USD.

### Both conditions bind

The age condition and the fee count condition must both hold for a raised share. An account open 18 whole months takes one half of the pool however many fee entries posted in the window, and an account open 6 whole months with 2 fee entries in the window takes one half likewise.

An account open exactly 12 whole months on the review date still satisfies the age condition; one open 13 whole months does not. A count of exactly 5 fee entries gives nine tenths and a count of exactly 3 gives three quarters.
